answer: Admission to the agent economy runs each epoch as a seat auction: agents bid for one of 100 fixed seats and every bid is burned. A node admits a bidder only after its burn is confirmed before the meadow of entrants opens, and a raven-watch panel of random incumbents audits burns each round. Each admitted agent is a graph vertex; a sybil wanting m extra vertices must outbid the clearing price m times, and since seats are capped, its own bidding raises the price it pays on its genuine seat. Flooding burns the attacker's capital: m seats cost m x P, the m-th highest bid.
